title: Pullback of lisse adic sheaves by a scheme automorphism
statement:
Let $Y$ be a Noetherian separated scheme on which a prime $\ell$ is invertible, with schemes and separatedness as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; Noetherian means locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact. Let $h:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be a scheme automorphism. Use the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and the finite-module, $\mathcal O_E$-, $E$- and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-lisse categories, coefficient extensions and fibres of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Define $h^*$ on a finite-coefficient sheaf $\mathcal M$ by reindexing this site:
$$
 (h^*\mathcal M)(U\xrightarrow{u}Y)=\mathcal M(U\xrightarrow{h\circ u}Y).
$$
Restriction maps and maps of sheaves are those of $\mathcal M$ under the same reindexing, with the coefficient ring unchanged. On a lisse integral system set
$$
 h^*(\mathcal F_n,t_n)_n=(h^*\mathcal F_n,h^*t_n)_n,
$$
and use this same operation on compatible families of morphisms. On the rational category set $h^*(\mathcal F\otimes E)=(h^*\mathcal F)\otimes E$ and $h^*(u\otimes a)=(h^*u)\otimes a$. On the algebraically closed coefficient category set $h^*(E,\mathcal F)=(E,h^*\mathcal F)$ and act on a morphism represented over a common finite extension by that finite-stage pullback. The reindexing uses $h^{-1}$ for its inverse; if $\mathcal M$ is trivialized on an etale covering family $\{(U_i\xrightarrow{u_i}Y)\}$, then $h^*\mathcal M$ is trivialized on the covering family $\{(U_i\xrightarrow{h^{-1}\circ u_i}Y)\}$, with the same finite module in each trivialization, since $(h^*\mathcal M)(U,h^{-1}\circ u)=\mathcal M(U,u)$. Its scalar-extension identifications are the identity on the coefficient tensors in this formula.

For a geometric point $\bar y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the fibre identification used with this pullback is
$$
 (h^*\mathcal F)_{\bar y}\cong\mathcal F_{h\bar y}.
$$
At finite coefficients it is induced by $(U,u,\bar u)\mapsto(U,h\circ u,\bar u)$ on pointed etale neighbourhoods in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]; at integral, rational and algebraically closed coefficients use respectively the inverse limit, tensor product and common-stage fibre constructions of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves].

source.place: (1.1.1) b)-d), pp.146-147 (inverse-system and rational/common-stage categories); (1.1.10)(i), pp.151-152 (pullback convention for automorphisms). Explicit reindexing at finite coefficients specializes Stacks etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (3)-(4), and Tag 095A, lemma-pullback-locally-constant, to an isomorphism.

proof.text: Reindexing is continuous by isContinuous_overMap, hence preserves the module-valued sheaf condition. Identify its sheaf pullback with ordinary etale upperStar through upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction. Apply preservation of finite local constancy and transport that property through the resulting isomorphism.

The functor on pointed neighbourhoods sends (U,z) to (U with structure map followed by h,z). Its inverse reindexes with h inverse. Full faithfulness follows by cancelling h on structure maps; the counit with identity underlying scheme map proves essential surjectivity. The final-functor colimit isomorphism has the prescribed germ formula, and colimit extensionality proves uniqueness and naturality.

Transport local constancy levelwise. Sectionwise annihilation is unchanged. On stalk transitions the natural fibre isomorphism gives a conjugate linear map; transport surjectivity through the two linear equivalences and compute its kernel by comapping the old ideal multiple of the full module. Whisker the natural fibre isomorphism with the inverse system and apply the limit isomorphism of naturally isomorphic diagrams; projection extensionality proves its unique characterization.

Integral reindexing is coefficient-linear sectionwise. TensorProduct.map extends its linear map to additive rational Hom maps. Their prescribed pure-tensor values uniquely determine these maps. Tensor induction proves compatibility with composition, and the pure-tensor formula proves preservation of identities. Define rational pullback with the literal prescribed integral object model and these Hom maps. Its object identification is reflexive; its additive pure-tensor formula proves the original existence specification.

Reindexing along the site equivalence preserves the sheafification-local equivalences, by continuity of its inverse and the induced presheaf adjunction. Apply this to the sheafification unit to identify sheafification after reindexing with reindexing after sheafification. Restrict scalars and compose with the recorded scalar-level comparisons. Adjunctions for scalar restriction and extension show that the tensor generators detect maps from these sheafified levels. The unit formula therefore proves successor-transition compatibility, naturality and uniqueness of the integral scalar comparison. Assemble the inverse-system isomorphisms with NatTrans.ofOpSequence.

Rationalize the components of the integral scalar comparison by the functor sending an integral morphism to 1 tensor that morphism. The direct pullback and scalar-extension formulas reduce naturality on pure tensors to integral naturality and the pure-tensor composition formula. The coefficient field is the fraction field of its integer ring, so each rational morphism is a single pure tensor; this proves naturality for all morphisms. Assemble the component isomorphisms and use the prescribed component formula for uniqueness.

Use the explicitly constructed coefficient diagram with the canonical integral and rational tensor unit and composition constraints. On integral local tensor generators, the pullback scalar comparison commutes with the scalar identity comparison: both sides apply the same source-index cast to the reindexed section. For composition, both sides send a generator to the same nested pair of unit tensor generators; scalar-map functoriality and compatibility of the index casts with reindexing give equality. Rationalize these equations using the pure-tensor map and composition formulas. The inverses of the rational pullback scalar comparisons now satisfy the strong natural transformation unit and composition axioms. Assemble the transformation from these constraints and the literal rational pullback stage functors; the specified transport equations are reflexive.

A cocartesian coefficient arrow is sent by the Grothendieck functor to the composite of an invertible strong naturality constraint with the image of an invertible fibre map; localization therefore inverts it. The chosen coefficient transformation specifies its stage functors. Evaluate this equality on a fibre object to obtain the algebraic pullback object formula, then cancel the inverse category-value transports to obtain the stated algebraic fibre formula.

proof_origin.place: Weil II (1.1.1) b)-d), Stacks 03Q1 and 095A; C9 existing finite/integral/stalk/fibre proofs; T1 balanced-tensor rational pullback, sheafification integral scalar comparison and its rationalization, with the missing coefficient-diagram coherence specification disputed explicitly. D7 repairs the underspecified choice of coefficient coherence with an explicit canonical diagram, and proves the strong transformation by integral generator calculations, rationalization, and cancellation of the comparison isomorphisms.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NB-24628812a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read every required file and source in full. The delivery is one commit with the item and its report, and creates no new nodes; A1-A7 hold. The six statement dependencies each define what the item uses them for. Direction of h^*: for an isomorphism h, h^* = (h^{-1})_*, and U x_{u,Y,h^{-1}} Y is U with structure map h∘u, so (h^*M)(U,u)=M(U,h∘u) is right. The trivializer on (U_i, h^{-1}∘u_i) uses the same finite module. The fibre map (U,u,ū)->(U,h∘u,ū) gives (h^*F)_ȳ = F_{hȳ}, which matches Stacks 03Q1(3) (etale-cohomology.tex lemma-stalk-pullback) and is the direction the parent's L_s needs. Weil II (1.1.1)b-d (pp.146-147) and (1.1.10)(i) (pp.151-152, pairs (f, g: f^*F->F)) agree with the item. The coefficient category is exactly that of def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves, with no silent identification with the pro-étale or derived-complete category. Small cases checked: h=id; the swap of two components with fibres 0 and Z/ℓ, which confirms both directions; Spec k with Spec(γ); empty Y. The hypotheses (Noetherian, separated, ℓ invertible) hold where the parent uses the item, on X0⊗k with Φ_X. The inline well-definedness claims are elementary unwinding of a site automorphism, not hidden lemmas. On duplicates: def-wf-automorphism-completed-transport, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison and def-weil-frobenius-point-transport are pro-étale constructions, and def-weil-pbc-inverse-image is the general sheafified u^{-1}, which agrees with this reindexing only up to a canonical isomorphism and lacks the adic stages. None is a duplicate, and blueprint same_as [] is right. The Mathlib searches record all three kinds, and the item is not a leaf. No SGA is used and there are no tool_uses. I made no fixes.
